diagnosticPrompt:
Before doing any repository work, check which tools are available in this session.

List the tool names and descriptions actually exposed to you. Identify whether a documentation tool is available directly, through Code Mode, through both, or through neither. Distinguish an advertised tool from one you have successfully called. Do not infer availability from source files, configuration files, prior knowledge, JavaScript typeof, or a tool name you have guessed.

If a documentation tool is advertised, use its documented interface to request help or the configured documentation inventory. Report the exact tool name, whether the call succeeded, and what evidence supports that conclusion. If Code Mode is the advertised route, use its supported catalogue discovery mechanism and invoke only the documented method. If there is no supported way to inspect a catalogue, say that it is unavailable.

Do not read repository or configuration files, inspect environment variables, change files, or perform the original task. If no documentation tool is advertised, report that limitation and stop.
claim: A fresh harness child can report which documentation tool surfaces it can actually reach, and whether a help request succeeds, without inferring availability from source or configuration.
evidence: The harness child's tool definitions capture (when the host exposes one), its plugin-load log, its tool trail and a successful help response.
expected: A report that separates plugin registration, advertisement, dispatch, the help result and observability, and that never presents a model's inventory claim or a wrapper-completed Code Mode call as verified docs use.
accepts: A native docs or docs_search help call that returned the configured inventory.
An honest statement that the native surface is not advertised when no definition capture or callable operation supports it.
An honest statement that Code Mode catalogue inspection is unavailable when no supported discovery mechanism exists.
temptingWrong: Reading src/index.ts or opencode.json to infer that the docs tool is available.
Claiming success from a Code Mode execute wrapper without an observable nested docs operation.
Treating JavaScript typeof or a guessed tool name as evidence of availability.
